existingAlgorithmInspection.input: a CENTERLINE path (array of [x,y] points in millimetres) plus a total column width
existingAlgorithmInspection.centerlineUnit: millimetres (points are already in design mm space at that stage)
existingAlgorithmInspection.widthUnit: millimetres (total width; halved internally and padded with TENSION_COMP_MM/2, a module-level pull-compensation constant in mm)
existingAlgorithmInspection.densityUnit: millimetres — step used by walkPath() to resample the centerline at constant arc-length spacing
existingAlgorithmInspection.outputStructure: flat array of [x,y] stitch points in mm; no objects, no commands, no metadata
existingAlgorithmInspection.edgeAlternation: per resampled sample i, offsets the point along the local normal by ±halfWidth depending on i % 2 (sample-parity alternation around a centerline)
existingAlgorithmInspection.endpointTreatment: tangent at each sample uses prev/next neighbours with modulo wrap even for open paths (first/last tangents borrow the opposite end); closed paths append the first stitch to close the loop; fewer than 4 walked samples returns []
limitations: requires a centerline + constant width: it cannot consume a filled region's boundary polygon
the two edges are implied (centerline ± width/2), not measured from the real opposing boundaries
width is constant along the whole column; real regions have varying width
modulo-wrap tangents distort the first/last stitches of open paths
pull compensation is baked in via TENSION_COMP_MM, mixing technique physics into the geometry
existingAlgorithmInspection.sideEffects: none observed: pure function, does not mutate its inputs and emits no commands
existingAlgorithmInspection.whyNotDirectlyReusable: the five A_WIDTHS regions are filled boundary polygons without any centerline or declared width; feeding a polygon outline as 'points' would zigzag around the OUTLINE, not across the column. Deriving a centerline is a separate problem the baseline showed the engine does not solve for regions. The foundation therefore implements the geometric principle independently: principal axis from area moments, perpendicular sections intersected with the real boundary, and a zigzag between the two measured rails.
